description: A game's opponent. Missing keys take their version's defaults.

policy.description: Who chooses moves. `llm`: the LLM alone. `systemone`: System 1 alone. `hybrid`: System 1 plays the moves it is confident about and suggests candidates otherwise.
policy.x-help: Who picks the moves: the LLM alone, System 1 alone, or System 1 with the LLM for the hard moves.

model.description: init_chat_model spec: `langsmith:<provider>/<model>` for the LLM Gateway, or `provider:model` and bare names with that provider's package installed.
model.x-help: The reasoning model that thinks through the positions System 1 hands over.

model_kwargs.description: Extra arguments for the model's constructor, as `init_chat_model` takes them: `temperature`, `max_tokens`, `extra_body` and so on. They win over every other setting. Credentials, connections, the model name and what the agent sends are held back. An output limit set only inside `extra_body` isn't seen, so memory may summarize too late.
model_kwargs.x-help: Extra arguments for the model, as JSON, such as {"temperature": 0.2}. They win over the settings here. A token limit set only inside extra_body isn't counted, so memory can summarize too late.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort passed to the model. Null sends none and uses the model's own default; models without reasoning (such as Claude Haiku 4.5) need it null.
reasoning_effort.x-help: How long the model thinks before it answers. Higher is slower and costs more. Leave it on the model's default for models without reasoning.

system_prompt.description: Replaces the bundled system prompt. Null keeps it. Each turn's message still ends by asking for `MOVE: <move>`; a reply without one is retried.
system_prompt.title: System Prompt
system_prompt.x-help: Replaces the instructions the model starts from. Leave it empty for the bundled prompt. Every turn still asks for a final MOVE line.

show_fen.description: Show the position's FEN in each turn's message. The moves so far are always shown, and so is the starting FEN of a game from another position.
show_fen.x-help: Include the position in FEN notation in every turn's message. Turn it off to see how the model does from the moves and the board alone.

show_board.description: Show the board as text in each turn's message.
show_board.x-help: Include a text drawing of the board in every turn's message. The moves so far are always shown.

move_list.description: The moves listed in each turn's message. `both`: System 1's candidates, when there are any, and every legal move. `legal`: every legal move. `candidates`: only the candidates. `none`: no list. A restricted turn always lists the permitted moves.
move_list.x-help: Which moves every turn's message lists: System 1's candidates, all legal moves, both, or none. Fewer lists mean a shorter prompt and a harder test.

memory.description: Keep earlier turns, summarized at 70% of the model's input limit. Needs a model with a known input limit. Ignored when the LLM doesn't play.
memory.x-help: Let the model see its earlier turns, summarized when the conversation gets long. Off, it sees only the current position, which is cheaper.

draw_claims.description: `auto` ends the game on a threefold repetition or the fifty-move rule; `never` plays on until a draw is forced.
draw_claims.x-help: End the game on a threefold repetition or after fifty moves without a capture or pawn move. Off, play continues until a draw is forced.

systemone_model.description: System 1 model: `semif-qwen3.5-4b` (SemIf) or `typesafe/jev-latest` (Jev). Another TypeSafe classifier works too, with a conservative cap on the moves per request.
systemone_model.x-help: The fast move ranker. It scores every legal move in about a second.

style.description: How each legal move is described to System 1. `rich` adds captures, checks and exchange results; `terse` names the move only.
style.x-help: How each move is described to System 1: with captures, checks and exchanges, or by name only.

with_eval.description: Also ask System 1 to score the position. Recorded only; it doesn't change the move.
with_eval.x-help: Also ask System 1 who stands better. It's recorded on the move and doesn't change what's played.

with_nouls.description: Also ask System 1 whether the position needs calculation and has tactics. Recorded only; it doesn't change the move.
with_nouls.x-help: Also ask System 1 whether the position needs calculation and has tactics. It's recorded on the move and doesn't change what's played.

gate.description: The signal compared with the threshold. `margin`: the top move's probability minus the second's. `confidence`: System 1's own confidence in its ranking.
gate.x-help: What System 1's confidence is judged by: how far its top move leads the next one, or its own confidence score.

threshold.description: System 1 plays its top move when the signal is at least this; otherwise the LLM gets its candidates. 0 always plays; 1 never does.
threshold.x-help: How confident System 1 must be to play a move without the LLM. Lower hands fewer moves to the LLM, which is faster and cheaper.

tournament_threshold.description: The threshold when there were more moves than one System 1 request holds, so they were ranked in a tournament. Null uses `threshold`.
tournament_threshold.title: Tournament Threshold
tournament_threshold.x-help: The same bar for positions with too many moves to rank at once, which System 1 ranks in rounds. Empty uses the bar above.

k.description: The most candidates suggested to the LLM.
k.x-help: How many of System 1's best moves the LLM is shown when System 1 isn't sure. The LLM can still play any legal move.

top_p.description: Cut the top `k` candidates further, to the fewest whose probabilities add up to at least this. Null keeps all `k`.
top_p.title: Top P
top_p.x-help: Show the LLM fewer candidates when the first few already cover this much of System 1's probability. Empty always shows them all.

seed.x-help: Makes System 1's rounds repeatable. Change it to replay a game with different luck.

title: Opponent
